title: How many nuts are in a serving? Grams and approximate counts

seo.title: How many nuts are in a serving? Grams and counts
seo.meta_description: A practical nut serving is about 1 ounce or 28–30 g. That is roughly 20–25 almonds, 15–20 cashews, 12–15 walnut halves, or 40–50 pistachio kernels.
seo.search_intent: Understand the gram weight and approximate piece count of a serving of common nuts and why counts vary.

excerpt: For comparing nuts, about 1 ounce or 28–30 grams of edible kernels is a useful reference. There is no fixed piece count: that weight can be roughly 20–25 almonds, 15–20 cashews, 12–15 walnut halves, or 40–50 pistachio kernels depending on size.
content_html:
Counting nuts is convenient, but individual pieces do not weigh the same. A practical serving reference is about 1 ounce, or roughly 28–30 g, of edible kernels. Piece counts are estimates built around that weight.

Approximate counts for 30 g

NutAbout 30 gApprox. calories
Almonds20–25 nuts~174
Cashews15–20 nuts~166
Walnuts12–15 halves~196
Pistachios, kernels40–50 kernels~168
Hazelnuts20–25 nuts~188

The ranges are intentionally broad because nut size varies. If precision matters, a kitchen scale is more reliable than memorizing a piece count.

Why 30 grams appears so often

FDA’s Reference Amount Customarily Consumed for whole, sliced, chopped, and slivered nuts and seeds is 30 g. FDA also notes that 1 ounce technically weighs 28.35 g, so household and metric label statements can look slightly different.

A serving is not 100 grams

Per-100-g tables are useful for comparisons, but 100 g of nuts commonly provides roughly 550–650 calories. A 30 g portion is closer to about 165–200 calories.

Walnuts, for example, are around 654 calories/100 g; 30 g is about 196 calories. The roughly 458-calorie difference is simply the effect of portion size.

Shell weight does not count as edible food

A 30 g nutrition serving refers to edible kernels. Thirty grams of in-shell pistachios is not 30 g of pistachio kernels because part of the measured weight is discarded.

Nut butter uses a different household measure

Nut butters are not counted by pieces. FDA’s reference amount for nut and seed butters is 2 tablespoons, and the gram weight varies by product. Labels often put two tablespoons near 30–32 g.

Your useful portion can be smaller or larger

Thirty grams is a reference, not a required dose. A 15 g sprinkle on oatmeal and a 40 g snack can both fit different meals and energy needs. The rest of the diet matters more than treating one ounce as a rigid rule.

The useful takeaway

Use roughly 1 ounce or 28–30 g of edible nuts as an easy comparison point. Piece counts are helpful for orientation, but weighing your usual variety once shows how much that serving actually looks like.

faq.question: How many almonds are in a serving?
faq.answer: Roughly 20–25 almonds often lands near 30 g, depending on almond size.

faq.question: How many walnut halves are in 1 ounce?
faq.answer: About 12–14 halves is a common approximation, with size variation.

faq.question: Is exactly 1 ounce required?
faq.answer: No. It is a useful reference amount, not a mandatory portion for everyone.
